name: Current transformer
summary: A current-measurement transformer used with metering and protection equipment.
description: A current transformer produces a secondary current related to the current in its primary conductor. A drawing uses the CT representation to show where current is measured and which metering or protection circuit receives that measurement. It does not, by itself, specify the CT ratio, accuracy class, burden or secondary connection.

On a single line diagram, the CT is placed at the measurement location. A schematic expands the secondary wiring, terminals and connected devices. Multi-core and multi-secondary CT arrangements require additional information; one generic preview cannot describe every configuration.
readingNotes: Follow the primary conductor through the CT and then identify the secondary circuit separately.
Polarity marks and terminal labels belong to the selected device and its documented connections.
drawingChecklist: Identify the metering or protection purpose.
Reference the ratio, class and burden in the equipment documentation.
Cross-reference secondary terminals and any test facility.
distinction: A CT measures current. A VT measures voltage. Their secondary circuits and isolation/testing arrangements are different.
